title.narrative: Lessons Learned - Documentation and dissemination of experiences in resilient rehabilitation of education and health infrastructure in Mozambique

description.narrative:
On September 29, 2015, the World Bank (WB) approved the Emergency Resilient Recovery Project (ERRP), in the amount of US$40 million to support early recovery of infrastructure, including education facilities damaged by storms and floods in central and northern Mozambique. This Project included dedicated technical assistance of UN-Habitat to help the Ministry of Education and Human Development (MINEDH) advance with the piloting of resilient recovery of education infrastructure, including the vulnerability and damage assessment, preparation of detailed designs and tender documents, and quality assurance of rehabilitation and construction of 700 classrooms in the provinces of Niassa, Zambezia and Nampula. As part of this pilot exercise, UN-Habitat has prepared technical guidelines for the resilient reconstruction of primary education following the “Building Back Better” approach.
UN-Habitat is currently supporting MINEDH with the scale up of resilient rehabilitation of education infrastructure covering 3,000 classrooms across the country under the World Bank-funded Mozambique Disaster Risk Management and Resilience Program (PforR). As part of this assignment, UN-Habitat has supported MINEDH and the Ministry of Public Works, Housing and Water Resources (MOPHRH) with the development of technical norms for reconstruction of education infrastructure which were approved through a joint ministerial diploma in October 2021.
Since 2021, the World Bank and UN Habitat are working collaboratively in the new agenda for building resilience to the health sector in Mozambique. On this regard, the WB completed the multi-hazards risk assessment on the health sector covering the entire public health network across the country, while UN-Habitat conducted a pilot vulnerability and damage assessment of selected health infrastructure as to test and refine a new methodology to inform the selection and prioritization of health infrastructure eligible for retrofitting.
From March 2023, UN-Habitat is co-chairing the Infrastructure Thematic Working Group on Planning Financing and Strategic Investment (PFEI), chaired by the Ministry of Health (MISAU), and with participation of different health partners interested in investing and/or implementing infrastructure projects in Mozambique.
Following the approval by the World Bank on May 4, 2023, of the activation of the Contingent Emergency Response Component (CERC) for response to impacts caused by cyclone Freddy across the country, UN-Habitat is being hired by to support MISAU and MINEDH with the vulnerability and damage assessment of health and education infrastructure affected by cyclone Freddy and preparation of detailed designs and biddings documents. The outcomes of this assignment are expected to build readiness for implementation of new World Bank operations currently under preparation in the Health and Disaster risk management sectors.
Starting on May 23, 2023, the WB has been implementing the Grant TF0C1614 “Enhancing Disaster Risk Management and Building Resilience in Mozambique's Health Infrastructure” which is supported by Global Facility for Disaster Risk Reduction (GFDRR) as part of the Japan-World Bank Program for Mainstreaming Disaster Risk Management in Developing Countries. This grant intends to provide support to the National Institute for Disaster Risk Management (INGD) and MISAU, specifically in relation to infrastructure management and strategic planning for mainstreaming disaster risk reduction throughout the lifecycle of Mozambique’s national health infrastructure in alignment with their strategic activities. Activities under this grant will particularly aim at increasing the understanding of the health sector's infrastructure vulnerability and challenges in terms of disaster risk reduction measures and methods to integrate risk information into decision processes; support MISAU in the design of an investment strategy and the identification of prioritized portfolios to address sector infrastructure needs to reduce disaster risk; and strengthen the institutional capacity of MISAU and needed tools to plan for health infrastructure considering disaster risk.
As part of the Grant TF0C1614, a consultancy is foreseen to document the process and lessons learned on vulnerability and damage assessment, selection of priority infrastructure, and preparation of detailed designs and bidding documents for resilient rehabilitation of education and health infrastructure in Mozambique.
World Bank aims to take advantage and maximize the experience acquired by UN-Habitat in Mozambique since 2002, and particularly, within the last 11 years in its engagement and technical assistance to the Government of Mozambique through the following sectors: i) Education and Human Development, ii) Health with focus on climate resilience and disaster risk reduction before, during and post-disaster.
